claim.claim-text: 1. A computer-implemented method comprising:
2. The computer-implemented method of claim 1 wherein both the SR prefix SID and the prefix are carried as network layer reachability information, NLRI, of a BGP update message,

wherein the BGP peer node preferably receives the FAD as a part of the BGP NLRI carrying the SR prefix SID and the prefix, wherein the BGP SR prefix SID is preferably encoded in a type length value, TLV, of the NLRI, and wherein the FAD is preferably encoded as a sub-TLV of the SR prefix SID TLV.
3. The computer-implemented method of any one of claims 1 and 2, further comprising:

determining, by the BGP peer node, whether or not it has a feasible path to the node identified by the prefix; and responsive to a determination that the BGP peer node has a feasible route to the node identified by the prefix carried in the SR prefix SID,

propagating reachability information for the prefix to an upstream BGP peer, and otherwise, responsive to a determination that the BGP node does not have a feasible route to the node identified by the prefix, not propagating reachability information for the prefix to the upstream BGP peer.

4. The computer-implemented method of any of claims 1 and 2, wherein the BGP peer node receives the FAD and a FAD identifier in a BGP link state, LS, node NLRI field of a BGP update message, and wherein SR prefix SID includes the FAD identifier, the computer-implemented method further comprising:

storing, by the BGP peer node, the FAD and the FAD identifier in its link state database; and responsive to receiving the SR prefix SID, finding the FAD stored in its link state database using the FAD identifier included in the SR prefix SID.
5. The computer-implemented method of claim 4 wherein the SR prefix SID is encoded in a TLV of a BGP NLRI field of a BGP update message.
6. The computer-implemented method of any of claims 1-5 wherein BGP is used to select feasible path(s) towards a peer node of a data center.
7. The computer-implemented method of any of claims 1-6 wherein the BGP peer node does not run an interior gateway protocol, IGP.
8. The computer-implemented method of any of claim 1-7 wherein the FAD includes at least one path computation constraint.

9. The computer-implemented method of any of claims 1-8 wherein the BGP peer node receives at least two FADs, and wherein the BGP peer node determines at least two different paths to the prefix carried in the SR prefix SID using the at least two FADs.
10. The computer-implemented method of any of claims 1-9 wherein the node identified by the prefix is a provider edge device, PE, for accessing a transport network.
11. A computer-readable medium storing processor executable instructions which, when executed by at least one processor, cause the at least one processor to perform a method comprising:

12. The computer-readable medium of claim 11 wherein the BGP peer node receives the FAD and a FAD identifier in a BGP link state, LS, node network layer reachability information, NLRI, field of a BGP update message, and wherein SR prefix SID includes the FAD identifier, the method further comprising:

storing, by the BGP peer node, the FAD and the FAD identifier in its link state database; and responsive to receiving the SR prefix SID, finding the FAD stored in its link state database using the FAD identifier included in the SR prefix SID.

receiving, by the BGP peer node, a segment routing, SR, prefix segment identifier, SID, associated with a prefix, receiving, by the BGP peer node, a flexible algorithm definition, FAD, determining, by the BGP peer node and using the FAD received, a next hop in a route towards a destination identified by the prefix, allocating a local label for the prefix, associating the local label with the determined next hop for the prefix, and storing, in a forwarding information base, FIB, of the BGP peer node, the next hop determined, wherein the act of storing, in the FIB of the BGP peer node, the next hop determined includes associating with the next hop, in the FIB, the prefix and the local label allocated.
14. The BGP peer node of claim 13 wherein both the SR prefix SID and the prefix are carried as network layer reachability information, NLRI, of a BGP update message.

15. The BGP peer node of claim 13 wherein the BGP peer node receives the FAD and a FAD identifier in a BGP link state, LS, node NLRI field of a BGP update message, and wherein SR prefix SID includes the FAD identifier, the method further comprising

storing, by the BGP peer node, the FAD and the FAD identifier in its link state database, and responsive to receiving the SR prefix SID, finding the FAD stored in its link state database using the FAD identifier included in the SR prefix SID.
